Photographs of a folder, with their species and their measured state

Source: R/measure_hub.R
measure_queue.Rd

Lists the photographs under photo_dir (sub-folders included), attaches a species to each, and says whether the landmark journal already holds a measurement of it. This is the table launch_measure_hub() is built on, exported so that a selection can be prepared or checked at the console.

Usage

measure_queue(photo_dir, species = NULL, journal_dir = NULL, exclude = NULL)

Arguments

photo_dir

Root folder of the photographs.

species

Where the species come from. NULL: unknown (NA). "folder": the name of the folder holding the photograph (one folder per species). A data.frame, or the path of a CSV / Excel file, with a column species and a column naming the photograph (photo, code, specimen, specimen_code or file, with or without extension), and optionally a column source (or data_source, provenance: campaign, museum, ...), which the hub's Results page filters on. Or a named character vector, code -> species.

journal_dir

Landmark journal of digitize_landmarks(), or a journal already read with landmark_journal_read(). NULL: no measured state (everything is "to measure").

exclude

Folders under photo_dir to leave out (for example the output of batch_landmarks(), whose control thumbnails are images too).

Value

A data.frame, one row per photograph: code, folder, subfolder, species, source (provenance, NA when the species table has none), file, path (absolute), measured, n_records (records in the journal: individuals, repeats), operator, timestamp, n_missing (expected points absent, worst individual), n_seeded (points never moved from their seed) and has_scale.

Details

The photograph's file name without its extension is the specimen code, as in digitize_landmarks(). Sub-folders are reported as two levels: folder (the first one under photo_dir) and subfolder (the rest of the path), so that a tree such as site/date/ or species/ can be browsed level by level.

See also

launch_measure_hub(), consolidate_landmarks(), landmark_journal_qc()

Examples

d <- file.path(tempdir(), "mq_demo", "Gobio occitaniae")
dir.create(d, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
for (f in file.path(d, c("GOBOCC_001.jpg", "GOBOCC_002.jpg"))) writeLines("x", f)
measure_queue(dirname(d), species = "folder")[c("code", "species", "measured")]
#>         code          species measured
#> 1 GOBOCC_001 Gobio occitaniae    FALSE
#> 2 GOBOCC_002 Gobio occitaniae    FALSE
